attribution.note: Marcus directly endorses the assertion about his seven predictions.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves the seven-of-seven retrospective assertion, assessed as of December 11, 2024. It does not independently resolve the underlying year-end forecasts.

contract.note: Reading the assertion as developments having borne out the predictions is ordinary and fair. The contract appropriately distinguishes durable deployment from experimentation and industry profits from individual losses, while acknowledging unspecified thresholds.

evidence.note: OpenAI's contemporaneous disclosure supports persistent hallucinations. It is company evidence, not an independent finding, and does not establish the other components.
Google's announced October price reductions support the pricing component within the target period. They do not establish industry profitability.
OpenAI's cheaper offering supports competitive pricing direction. A new small model does not establish matched price reductions across frontier providers.

The dated survey supports competitive alternatives and weakening incumbent advantage. Reported production use and capability gains provide counterweight, but do not establish durable adoption levels, a major breakthrough, or the absence of all moats.
The contemporaneous survey measures worker uptake and work-hour intensity. Rapid uptake merits consideration, but neither measure settles durable corporate deployment.

reviews.rationale: Pricing reductions and persistent hallucinations have support; competitive alternatives have partial support. Model count, absence of a major advance, overall moat strength, durable adoption and industry profits remain unsettled. Reported deployment and rapid worker uptake do not clearly falsify the adoption component. The packet neither establishes all seven nor clearly falsifies one.
